role_place: Byzantine monk and chronicler (Greek-speaking, Constantinople region); author of the Chronographia (place of monastery not checked).
why_relevant: Earliest Greek narrative in the set that describes Muhammad's marriage (to Khadija) and mentions Abu Bakr as his successor; does not name Aisha.
fame: Very well known: the Chronographia is a main Byzantine chronicle for 602-813 and a key source for early Byzantine-Arab relations.
community: Byzantine Greek Orthodox (monk, confessor of icons)

role_place: Monk, author of an Elenchus (refutation of the 'Agarenes') and a Contra Muhammed; place and date not fixed in the sources read.
why_relevant: Only Greek text read so far that names Aisha in the Greek-Latin edition (as Aise / Ἀϊσέ in the list of four wives) and gives a critical list of Muhammad's wives and concubines.
fame: Little known; the Elenchus was edited by Stephanus Le Moyne (Lugdunum Batavorum 1685) and reprinted in PG 104.
community: Greek Christian (Orthodox or Melkite; not determined from the edition)

role_place: Byzantine monk in Constantinople, author of the Panoplia dogmatica (Titulus XXVIII, 'Adversus Saracenos').
why_relevant: Greek text with Latin facing that criticises Muhammad's law of four wives and concubines; does not name Aisha.
fame: Known to specialists of Byzantine heresiology and Byzantine-Muslim polemic; the Panoplia is widely cited.

role_place: Byzantine historian and imperial official in Constantinople; author of the Thesaurus orthodoxae fidei, book XX on the Agarenes.
why_relevant: Greek text (with Latin facing in PG 140) describing Muhammad's four legal wives, the concubines and the Zayd episode as criticism; no Aisha name, no age.
fame: Very well known as a Byzantine historian (Historia); the Thesaurus is less read.
